The Body Coach app review: workouts, recipes, support and value

A research-based review of the workout and recipe experience, support and ongoing cost.

By Nutrition.Fitness · 15 September 2026 · 4 min read

The short answer

The Body Coach app may suit you if you want structured workouts and recipes together and enjoy Joe Wicks’s approach. Its checkout showed £14.99 monthly or £89.99 annually on 15 September 2026, while a marketing page advertised a £69.99 September annual offer. Check the offer and renewal terms. This is a research-based review, not hands-on testing.

The Body Coach app is worth considering if you want guided workouts and recipes together, and you enjoy Joe Wicks's style of encouragement. Its published offer is broader than a workout-video library. Whether it represents good value depends on how comfortably the exercise schedule, recipes and presentation fit your week.

This is a research-based review, not hands-on testing. We checked official information on 15 September 2026. Nutrition.Fitness is developing NUFI, which competes for some of the same buyers. We are not an independent testing laboratory, and we have not assessed workout delivery, recipe taste or support response times.

What is the actual price?

Published optionPrice foundImportant distinction
Monthly£14.99 per month12 payments total £179.88
Standard annual£89.99 per yearOne annual payment; about £7.50 a month equivalent
September annual offer£69.99 advertisedPromotional marketing price; confirm eligibility and checkout total

The subscription page showed the standard monthly and annual figures. The how-it-works page advertised a September annual reduction. We are showing that difference rather than pretending the lower price is available to every account. Check the amount due today and the later renewal price.

The monthly option displayed a seven-day free trial; the checkout also states subscriptions renew unless cancelled. Do not assume every annual offer includes the same trial. On the standard figures, six monthly payments total £89.94, almost the annual fee. Monthly can cost more over a full year while still being sensible when you are unsure of the fit.

What do workouts and recipes include?

The official plan explanation describes workout cycles based on starting ability and recipes with calculated portions. Its homepage FAQ lists short workout options, mixed and plant-based meal-plan choices, and community access. It also says many workouts need no equipment, with dumbbells needed as users progress into intermediate and advanced plans.

That combination could help if your difficulty is deciding both what to cook and which session to do. The useful question is whether having those choices made for you feels supportive. Someone who already follows a lifting programme and loves their usual meals may need much less.

Check a normal week, not an imaginary one

Write down the days you could realistically exercise, including changing and clearing floor space. Then check the programme against those days. A session described as short still has to fit between work, dinner and the school bag that mysteriously needs finding again.

Inspect a sample recipe against your cupboards and your household. Would everyone eat a version of it? Could leftovers cover tomorrow's lunch? Does the cooking time include preparation? A meal can be appealing and still be the wrong Wednesday-night choice.

If you choose an available trial, use it to answer practical questions rather than chase a dramatic before-and-after result. Can you follow the instructions comfortably? Are modifications suitable for you? Is the next session easy to find? Can you swap a meal without creating extra work? We have not tested these points, so they are questions for your own evaluation.

What does “support” mean?

Community encouragement and customer support can be valuable. They should not be read as a promise that Joe personally reviews your technique or that an individual professional monitors your health. If that level of help is essential, ask precisely who responds, what they can advise on and how contact works before purchasing.

A polished demonstration does not tell a trainer how you are moving at home. If you need exercise adapted around an injury or condition, seek an appropriately qualified professional who can assess your circumstances. Do not buy a general app on the assumption that it includes individual rehabilitation.

Who should choose it, and who might pass?

Shortlist The Body Coach if its teaching style makes you want to return, you like structured home sessions and its recipes fit your household. Consider a focused diary if food logging is the only missing piece. Consider a trainer if direct observation and personal adaptation are your priorities. Free workouts and a simple written meal plan remain valid options when money is tight.

NUFI's listed prices are £29.99 monthly or £99 paid annually. We cannot justify either by claiming more buttons or a better result without evidence. Our current site is a preview with login and payment not connected; compare the offer and billing basis on that understanding.

Choose the approach you can picture using after a tiring day. Before deciding, identify the one feature you would miss most if it disappeared. That is a better starting point for value than a discount banner.

Sources and checks

Information checked on 15 September 2026. Prices, availability and subscriptions can change; check the linked provider before paying.
